He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale Bulldogs]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. At Yale, he earned 2024 first-team All-[[Ivy League]] honors, the [[2024 Ivy League men's basketball tournament|2024 Ivy League tournament]] [[most valuable player|MVP]], and led the league in rebounds and blocks per game. At Michigan, he was a second-team All-Big Ten selection in 2025, leading the conference in rebounds per game and double-doubles. He competed for [[Israel men's national under-20 basketball team|Israel]] at the [[2023 FIBA U20 European Championship]], winning a [[silver medal]] and earning all-tournament team honors. ==Early and personal life== Wolf was born in [[Glencoe, Illinois]], in the United States.{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/danny-wolf/19240|title=Danny Wolf – 2023–24 – Men's Basketball|website=Yale University}} His oldest brother, Josh, played basketball at [[Lehigh University]], and his other older brother, Jake, plays basketball at [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. His father is 6' 8" and his mother is 5' 10".{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/07/09/after-a-series-of-growth-spurts-lake-forest-academys-danny-wolf-hits-6-10-and-starts-receiving-division-i-offers-on-the-first-day-it-was-the-coolest-thing-ever/|title=After a series of growth spurts, Lake Forest Academy's Danny Wolf hits 6-10 and starts receiving Division I offers on the first day: 'It was the coolest thing ever.'|first=Bobby |last=Narang|date=July 9, 2020|work=The Chicago Tribune}} Danny is 7 feet (2.13 m) tall and weighs 250 pounds (113 kg). ==High school career== Wolf attended [[Lake Forest Academy]] for three years before transferring to [[Northfield Mount Hermon School]] for his senior year, where he helped the team reach the finals in both the NEPSAC Triple-A championship and the national prep championship. Under his leadership, the team was ranked number 11 in the country for the majority of the season. Additionally, he received a [[McDonald's All-American Game]] nomination, and was a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/minnesota/Article/Minnesota-Basketball-Recruiting-Danny-Wolf-Ben-Johnson-166669458/|title=2022 PF Danny Wolf discusses his Minnesota official visit|website=247Sports|author=Ryan James|date=June 17, 2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/11/12/recruiting-notes-6-foot-10-junior-danny-wolf-cites-uncertainty-in-illinois-opportunity-on-east-coast-in-decision-to-transfer-from-lake-forest-academy/|title=Recruiting notes: 6-foot-10 junior Danny Wolf cites uncertainty in Illinois, opportunity on East Coast in decision to transfer from Lake Forest Academy|author=Bobby Narang |work=Chicago Tribune|date=November 12, 2020}}{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/college-prospect-spotlight-yales-danny-wolf-#:~:text=Notable%20Accolades,experience%20at%20the%20college%20level|title=College Prospect Spotlight: Yale's Danny Wolf; This week, we highlight the spectacular play of Yale center Danny Wolf|date=December 21, 2023|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=February 21, 2024}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] because of the elite combination of academics and basketball that the school provided.{{cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/danny-wolf/19240|title=Men's Basketball Roster – Danny Wolf|last=|date=October 27, 2023|website=[[Yale]]|access-date=February 21, 2024}} ==College career== ===Yale=== In his freshman season at [[Yale University]], 2022–23, Wolf primarily played for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Bulldogs]] as a backup to forwards [[EJ Jarvis]], Isaiah Kelly, and Matt Knowling, averaging 2.6 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.4 blocks. His best performances came in the final two games of the regular season, where he averaged seven points, five rebounds, one steal and one block. After the season, he received Yale's John C. Cobb Award, which is given to the team’s rookie of the year. At the start of his sophomore season, 2023–24, Wolf moved into a starting role and became the focal point of the Bulldogs’ offense.{{Cite web|url=https://bvmsports.com/2024/01/03/yale-vs-howard-sophomore-sensation-danny-wolf-leads-bulldogs-as-6-point-favorites-in-college-basketball-showdown/|title=Yale vs. Howard: Sophomore sensation Danny Wolf leads Bulldogs as 6-point favorites in college basketball showdown|date=January 3, 2024|website=BVM Sports}}{{Cite web|url=https://ivyleague.com/news/2024/1/22/mens-basketball-wolf-mack-repeat-ivy-mens-hoops-weekly-winners.aspx|title=Wolf, Mack Repeat as Ivy Men's Hoops Weekly Award Winners|date=January 22, 2024|website=ivyleague.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2024/02/15/dom-amore-danny-wolf-weirdly-unbelievable-adds-new-dimension-to-yales-basketball-aspirations/|author=Dom Amor|title= Danny Wolf, 'weirdly unbelievable,' adds new dimension to Yale's basketball aspirations|date=February 15, 2024|work=Harford Courant}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.ctinsider.com/college/article/danny-wolf-yale-mens-basketball-ivy-league-18641768.php|title=Danny Wolf powers Yale basketball team to six-game winning streak|work=CT Insider|date=February 1, 2024|first=Myer|last=Lee}} On November 19, 2023, he posted then-career-highs 21 points, 11 rebounds and four assists in an overtime win over [[Gardner-Webb University]]. Wolf’s play earned him the Ivy League Player of the Week five times, including three straight from January 23, 2024, to February 12.{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/2/12/mens-basketball-wolf-earns-ivy-player-of-week-honors-for-fifth-time.aspx|title=Wolf Earns Ivy Player of Week Honors for Fifth Time|date=February 12, 2024|website=Yale University}}{{cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/2/12/mens-basketball-wolf-earns-ivy-player-of-week-honors-for-fifth-time.aspx#:~:text=Wolf%2C%20who%20scored%2025%20points,awards%20in%20a%20single%20season|title=Wolf Earns Ivy Player of Week Honors for Fifth Time|last=Bennett|first=Tim|date=February 12, 2024|website=Yale Athletics|access-date=February 21, 2024}} During that stretch, he averaged 17.6 points, 10.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.8 blocks, leading the Bulldogs to an undefeated record during the span. Wolf became just the seventh player in Ivy League history to earn five Player of the Week awards in a single season. In 2023–24, Wolf led the [[Ivy League]] with 310 rebounds, 247 defensive rebounds, 9.7 rebounds per game, and 1.3 blocks per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/danny-wolf-1.html|title=Danny Wolf College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} He finished the year averaging 14.1 points per game (10th in the league), had 43 blocks (second), 63 offensive rebounds, 176 field goals (third), a .472 field goal percentage (fourth) and 33 steals (tenth). He earned unanimous first team All-Ivy honors and a [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] District 13 first-team selection, as well as being named the most outstanding player in the Ivy League tournament.{{Cite web|url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2024/3/20/mens-basketball-wolf-jones-finalists-for-collegeinsider-awards.aspx|title=Wolf, Jones Finalists for CollegeInsider Awards|date=March 20, 2024|website=Yale University}} ===Michigan=== On April 20, 2024, Wolf transferred to the [[University of Michigan]] to play for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Wolverines]] in the [[Big Ten Conference]].{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2024/04/20/danny-wolf-transfer-portal-michigan-basketball-yale-dusty-may-commitment-height/73398502007/|title=7-foot Yale transfer Danny Wolf commits to Dusty May, Michigan basketball|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|first=Craig|last=Meyer|date=April 20, 2024|access-date=April 22, 2024}} On November 4, 2024, in his first game with Michigan against [[2024–25 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team|Cleveland State]], Wolf led all players with 19 points and 13 rebounds, while adding three blocks, three steals and two assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401707875/cleveland-st-michigan|title=Michigan v. Cleveland State (November 4, 2024)|website=[[ESPN.com]]}} In the seventh game of the season against [[2024–25 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]], Wolf had his third double-double of the season, leading all players with 20 points and 14 rebounds as Michigan became the [[Fort Myers Tip-Off]] champions.{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/11/27/michigan-basketball-takes-down-no-22-xavier-to-win-fort-myers-tip-off-title/76619810007/|title=Michigan basketball routs No. 22 Xavier to win Fort Myers Tip-Off title|work=[[The Detroit News]]}} In the next game against [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]], Wolf scored 20 points, grabbed a team-high seven rebounds and recorded a game-high five assists, three steals and five blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/03/michigan-basketball-stuns-wisconsin-67-64-despite-frigid-1st-half/76752779007/|title= 7-footers lift Michigan basketball after brutal start to 67-64 upset of No. 11 Wisconsin|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]}} On January 4, 2025 against [[2024–25 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]], Wolf had 21 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists and a career-high six blocks, earning his seventh double-double of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=401721330 |title=Michigan v. USC (January 4, 2025) |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 4, 2025 |access-date=January 4, 2025}} On January 16 against [[2024–25 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]], Wolf scored a season-high 23 points with ten rebounds and seven assists; his eighth double-double with Michigan.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401721359/michigan-minnesota|title=Michigan v. Minnesota (January 16, 2025)|website=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 5 against [[2024–25 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]], he had 15 points and 12 rebounds, leading all Big Ten players with ten double-doubles through 22 games.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/2/5/mens-basketball-u-m-holds-off-late-charge-to-secure-pink-game-victory-over-oregon |title=U-M Holds Off Late Charge to Secure Pink Game Victory Over Oregon |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=February 5, 2025 |access-date=February 5, 2025}} In March, Wolf was named a finalist for the [[Karl Malone Award]], given to the nation’s best [[power forward]] each season.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/03/06/michigan-basketball-danny-wolf-finalist-for-best-power-forward/81778324007/ |title=Danny Wolf named finalist for Karl Malone Award as nation's best PF |website=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Tony Garcia|date=March 6, 2025}} He also earned second-team All-Big Ten honors, selected by both the coaches and media,{{cite web|url=https://umhoops.com/2025/03/11/vlad-goldin-earns-first-team-all-big-ten-honors-wolf-named-to-second-team/ |title=Goldin earns First Team All-Big Ten honors, Wolf named to Second Team |website=UM Hoops |author=Dylan Burkhardt |date=March 11, 2025 |access-date=March 11, 2025}} and was named to the all-tournament team after leading Michigan to a Big Ten championship in the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2025 Big Ten tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/16/mens-basketball-michigan-wins-2025-big-ten-tournament-championship-over-wisconsin |title=U-M Downs No. 18 Wisconsin to Capture B1G Tournament Title |first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}} He was joined by teammate [[Vlad Goldin]], [[Derik Queen]], [[John Blackwell (basketball)|John Blackwell]] and [[John Tonje]].{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/blt76f5fa6f38409be3/|title=Michigan Claims 2025 TIAA Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament Title|accessdate=March 17, 2025|date=March 16, 2025|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]}} In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]], Wolf was named to the south regional all-tournament team, along with [[Johni Broome]], [[Tahaad Pettiford]], [[Jase Richardson]] and [[Sean Pedulla]].{{cite web|url=https://auburnwire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/auburn/mens-basketball/2025/03/31/auburn-basketball-march-madness-all-south-team-johni-broome-tahaad-pettiford/82737959007/|title=Auburn duo earns NCAA Tournament All-South Region team honors|accessdate=April 1, 2025|date=March 31, 2025|publisher=[[USA Today]]|author=Jones, Taylor}} As a junior, Wolf averaged 13.2 points, 9.7 rebounds, 3.6 assists, and 1.4 blocks per game. He led the Big Ten in rebounding and in double-doubles, finishing in a tie with [[Julian Reese]] and Derik Queen with 15 double-doubles.{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/stats/?sortBy=REB |title=2024-25 Big Ten Rebounds Per Game Leaders |website=[[Big Ten]] |date=April 1, 2025 |access-date=April 1, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/556 |title=Men’s Basketball NCAA Division I Double Doubles (2024-25) |website=[[NCAA]] |date=April 1, 2025 |access-date=April 1, 2025}} On April 16, Wolf announced he would forgo his senior season and declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://africa.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44699616/michigan-danny-wolf-enter-nba-draft-forgo-ncaa-eligibility |title=Michigan's Danny Wolf to enter NBA draft, forgo NCAA eligibility |newspaper=[[ESPN.com]] |first=Jonathan |last=Givony |date=April 16, 2025 |access-date=April 16, 2025}} ==Team Israel career== While from the United States, Wolf’s Jewish background and heritage allow him to compete for team Israel as a [[naturalized citizen]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/j-spot/article-749199|title=Yale hoopster Danny Wolf checks in ahead of representing Israel at U20 Euro|last=Halickman|first=Joshua|date=July 7, 2023|website=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|access-date=February 21, 2024}} In his first national-level competition, Wolf represented
